newsitem.title: USA: Michael Foods sees Q2 above expectations.
newsitem.headline: Michael Foods sees Q2 above expectations.

text.p: Michael Foods Inc on Thursday said it expected second-quarter earnings to exceed the current consensus estimate of $0.23 a share by at least 50 percent.

"Consensus EPS expectations are at $0.23 for the quarter, versus $0.17 a year ago, and we expect to exceed that level of estimated earnings by at least 50 percent based upon the information available to us today," Gregg Ostrander, chief executive, said in a statement.
To be sure, he cautioned, second-quarter results are not necessarily indicative of the rest of the year.

"While we are obviously pleased by the strength in earnings experienced year to date, we wish to caution analysts and investors from rushing to extrapolate the recent earnings trend into the future," Ostrander said.
"In part, it is likely that egg industry market conditions are not sustainable at this level," he said.

"Also, while the corn and soybean crops are off to a good start, there is much uncertainty about the ultimate outcome of these crops, and these grains are a major cost component for us relative to feeding our flocks," he added.
In the second quarter, Ostrander said, the operating environment in the egg industry, food cost improvements and overall volume trends for value-added products have all been favorable.
Michael Foods processes and distributes egg products, refrigerated grocery products, specialty dairy products and refrigerated potato products.
